transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess I came because I’ve been doing some odd things at church. Like at the potluck, I’ll just stand there holding the serving spoon up and not move, or I keep folding the same napkins again and again while folks are waiting. It’s… embarrassing.
Do you find yourself repeating certain movements or actions over and over without meaning to, even when you’re not at church or in social situations?

Mostly it’s at church that I notice it. I’ll be there by the potluck table and just… hold the serving spoon up, not moving, or I keep folding the same napkins over and over while folks are waiting. I don’t really know why I do it.
Do you ever find yourself repeating certain movements or behaviors, like tapping, blinking, or touching things over and over, even when you’re not at church or around other people?

I don’t know about tapping or blinking… not really. It’s more like what I said, at church I’ll get stuck holding the serving spoon up, or I’ll fold the same napkins over and over while people are waiting. It feels odd to say.
Do you ever find yourself repeating movements or behaviors like holding objects in place or folding things over and over when you’re at home or by yourself?

I don’t know so much when I’m by myself… I mostly notice it at church. Like I said, I’ll be by the potluck table holding the serving spoon up and just not moving, or folding the same napkins again and again while people are waiting. It’s embarrassing.
When you're not at church, do you ever feel anxious, upset, or have trouble functioning normally during the day?

I… I manage most days, I guess. But I did have to step back from some choir things and helping at church, because I mix up plans sometimes. Then people get uncomfortable, or they have to redo what I was supposed to do. It’s… hard to talk about.

When you’re at home, alone or not in a social setting, do you ever catch yourself repeating movements or behaviors without meaning to—like holding objects still, tapping, or doing something over and over again?

At home… I don’t really notice it the same way. It’s mostly what brought me in—at church, by the potluck table, I’ll get stuck holding the serving spoon up, or folding the same napkins over and over while people are waiting. It’s embarrassing.

Have you ever noticed yourself making movements that you can’t control—like sudden twitches, jerks, or repeated actions—when you’re not at church, even if just small things like blinking or shrugging your shoulders?

I don’t know about twitches or blinking so much. It’s more… what I already said, at church I get stuck doing odd things—holding the serving spoon up by the potluck table, or folding the same napkins while people are waiting. It’s embarrassing.
When you're not at church, do you ever notice yourself making small, involuntary movements—like blinking, shrugging, or tapping—without meaning to?
I… I can’t say I’ve noticed that, no. Not the blinking or shrugging kind of thing. If it happens, I don’t really catch it.

Have you ever had any sudden, quick movements or sounds that you couldn’t control, like coughing randomly, making a face, or clearing your throat without meaning to—even if it was just for a short time?
No… I don’t think so. Not like coughing or making faces that I can’t stop. I haven’t really noticed anything like that.
When you're not at church, do you ever feel like you have to do something over and over, like checking, counting, or arranging things in a certain way, even if you don't want to?
I don’t really think so. I mean… I check things sometimes like anyone, but not where I feel I have to keep doing it over and over. Not that I’ve noticed.
Outside of what you've described at church, do you ever feel a strong need to do certain things a specific way or in a certain order, even if you don’t really want to?
Not really… I don’t think I have anything like that. I just do things the usual way, but I don’t feel like I have to, no.

Outside of being at church, have you ever felt a strong urge or need to do something over and over again, even if you didn’t want to, like touching things a certain number of times or organizing items in a specific way?
No… I can’t say I do that. I don’t have to touch things a certain way or line things up or anything like that, not that I’ve noticed.

Before you find yourself doing those repeated actions at church, like holding the spoon or folding napkins, do you ever feel a strong inner tension, discomfort, or a need to do it—even if you’re not exactly aware why?

I don’t know if it’s tension exactly. It’s more like… I just end up doing it. At church, by the potluck table, I’ll be holding the serving spoon up and not moving, or folding the same napkins again and again while people are waiting. I can’t really explain why.
Before you start doing those repeated actions at church, like holding the spoon or folding napkins, do you ever feel a strange urge or inner discomfort that makes you feel like you have to do it?

I’m not sure it feels like an urge, exactly. I just… I’ll be there at the potluck table and then I’m holding the serving spoon up, not moving, or folding the same napkins again while people are waiting. I don’t really know why I start.
Have you ever had experiences where you saw, heard, or felt things that others around you didn’t seem to notice?
I don’t know… I haven’t really noticed anything like that. Not that I can say for sure.
Have you ever found yourself sitting or standing completely still for long periods, not responding to others, or moving in a very strange or unusual way, even if just for a short time?

Yes… I guess that happens at church. I’ll be standing there by the potluck table holding the serving spoon up, just not moving for a while. Or I keep folding the same napkins over and over, even when people are waiting. I don’t really mean to do it.
Have you ever experienced times when you felt frozen or unable to move, or moved in a very strange or robotic way, even when you weren’t at church or around other people?

Mostly what I know is at church… by the potluck table. I’ll stand there holding the spoon up and just not move, or I’ll keep folding the same napkins while people are waiting. I don’t really know about other times.
Have you ever felt frozen or unable to move, or moved in a very strange or robotic way when you’re not at church or around other people?

I don’t really know about when I’m by myself. What I came about is… at church, I’ll just stand there with the serving spoon up, not moving, or keep folding the same napkins while people are waiting. That’s what I notice.
Have you ever felt frozen or unable to move, or moved in a very strange or robotic way when you’re not at church or around other people?

I… I don’t know about other places. What I notice is at church, by the potluck table. I’ll be holding the serving spoon up and just stop, or keep folding the same napkins over and over while people are waiting.
